name: Feegow
tagline: Brazilian clinic management suite: scheduling, electronic patient records, billing and health insurer claims in one system.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: An agent can absolutely build you a calendar with patients attached to it, and for a solo practitioner keeping private notes that might even be pleasant. What it cannot build is the part clinics actually pay for: electronic medical records that satisfy CFM and SBIS expectations, digital signing with ICP-Brasil certificates, TISS-format claim submission to Brazilian health insurers, LGPD-grade audit trails, and NF-e issuance. Those are not features, they are specifications maintained by other people who change them without asking you. Add the fact that a clinic has receptionists, dentists, doctors and a finance person all touching the same records with different permissions, and the DIY version stops being a personal replacement. The honest consolation is a local scheduler plus patient notes for one practitioner who bills cash.
coreLoopDIY: A local single-practitioner app that books appointments on a calendar and keeps a running per-patient record of visits, notes and payments in SQLite.
requirements: a machine that stays on if anyone else needs to see the calendar
a backup habit, because this is health data with no safety net
a real system if you ever bill insurers
whatYouLose: TISS claim generation and submission to Brazilian health insurers, which is the whole billing pipeline for most clinics
Digital signature of records with ICP-Brasil certificates, and any credible claim of CFM/SBIS compliance
Multi-role access control and audit logging that survives an LGPD question
Fiscal invoicing, payment integrations and financial reporting the accountant expects
Patient-facing confirmations by WhatsApp and SMS, plus a support line when the receptionist is stuck at 8am
moatNotes: Brazilian healthcare software lives inside TISS, CFM, SBIS and LGPD. None of those are things you implement once and forget.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because a clinic is not one person with a calendar. It is a front desk, several practitioners, a finance seat, insurer claims that must be formatted exactly right or they get rejected, and medical records that a regulator or a lawyer may one day read closely. Paying a vendor moves the burden of tracking specification changes and staying compliant off your desk, and gives you someone to call when the receptionist cannot check in a patient. Self-hosting patient health data on your own box for a real practice is a liability decision, not a technical one.
notes: A scheduler with patient notes is a weekend; a clinic system is not. The moat is TISS, CFM and LGPD, three specifications you do not control and cannot ignore.
prompt:
Build a local, single-practitioner clinic scheduler and patient log. Not a clinic management system, no insurer billing, no compliance claims.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Next.js 14 App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, file at ./data/clinic.db
- Zod for validation, date-fns for dates
- Runs with `npm run dev` on localhost only, no auth, no cloud, no telemetry, no analytics

Data model:
- patient: id, full name, birth date, phone, email, notes, created_at
- appointment: id, patient_id, starts_at, duration_min, service label, status (scheduled | done | no_show | cancelled), price_cents, paid (bool)
- record_entry: id, patient_id, appointment_id nullable, written_at, body text (append only, entries are never edited or deleted, only superseded by a new entry that references the old id)

Screens:
1. Week view calendar, Mon to Sat, 07:00 to 20:00 in 30 minute slots. Click an empty slot to book: search existing patient by name or create one inline. Drag is not required, an edit dialog is fine.
2. Day list for the front desk: today's appointments in order, one click to mark done, no_show or cancelled, one click to mark paid.
3. Patient page: contact details, appointment history, and the append only record entries newest first, with a box to add a new entry.
4. Money page: sum of paid and unpaid appointments per month, plus a CSV export of all appointments.

Rules:
- Prevent double booking the same time range, show a clear inline error.
- Store all money as integer cents, format in BRL.
- Store timestamps as ISO strings in UTC, render in local time.
- Add `npm run backup` that copies clinic.db to ./backups/clinic-YYYY-MM-DD-HHmm.db.
- Seed script with 8 fake patients and 20 appointments across the current week.

Explicitly out of scope, do not build or stub: TISS claim files, insurer integrations, ICP-Brasil digital signatures, NF-e issuance, WhatsApp or SMS reminders, multi-user roles, payment gateways, telehealth.

End with a README that lists the commands and states in plain language that this stores health data unencrypted on the local disk, has no access control, and is not suitable for a multi-practitioner clinic or for insurer billing.
